long_biography.plain_text:
Hawatt began in international trade and advisory work before joining SAE Institute as a consultant in the late 1990s. He took broader management responsibility as the creative-media education group expanded internationally, later serving as chief executive and chair of its governing council. He led the transaction process culminating in Navitas' acquisition, then stayed through the transition before departing in 2014.

A longstanding interest in flying shaped his next platform. Hawatt established a global aviation-training brand, developing academies for civilian and military pilots, cabin crew, ground staff and maintenance engineers. The network now operates across several regions with aircraft and simulator capacity, while his wider Dubai investment group retains interests in property, destination management and charter services. He also advocates against trafficking and modern slavery.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 100: the authoritative exact name and current Riana relationship converge with Hawatt's direct acknowledgment of Riana, Arab News' independent boat attribution, a current brochure naming Romy Hawatt at the Riana Group email domain, and official Riana Group and Airways Aviation founder profiles.

The authoritative input records Riana at 41 metres and 223 GT, while the recent brochure presents it as 42 metres and 220 GT. The exact vessel name, Silyon builder, Romy Hawatt contact and rianagroup.com email show this is the same vessel; the numerical difference likely reflects measurement conventions or later documentation, but no unsupported reconciliation is asserted.

A 2025 brochure markets Riana for sale. The authoritative current relationship remains the immutable baseline for this dossier, while the listing and any possible later transaction are excluded from both biographies so the copy remains sale-independent.

Hawatt did not found SAE Institute. Navitas records SAE's 1976 founding and its 2011 entry into Navitas, while corporate sources establish Hawatt's later chief-executive, governing-chair and transaction-leadership roles. The biographies use senior stewardship rather than founder language.

The A$289 million figure was Navitas' enterprise acquisition price for SAE Group. No reliable source reviewed identifies Hawatt's equity interest, vendor consideration or personal proceeds, so the amount is not presented as his wealth or used to estimate net worth.

Diversified is the most defensible original wealth-creation classification because Hawatt's direct answer identifies property, international trade and import-export, alongside a material education-management career. Public evidence does not quantify the relative contribution of those fields. Aviation & Aerospace is independently clearer as his current defining industry.

Self-made — independent start reflects founder-built current groups and the absence of any documented inherited business or dynastic transfer. Public sources do not disclose all early financing or SAE ownership economics, so the confidence remains high rather than very high.

Founder is the appropriate current relationship because official sources identify Hawatt as founder of both Riana Group and Airways Aviation. His former relationship to SAE was operator and transaction leader and is not allowed to blur that distinction.

Aviation is the minimum useful approved tag. Pilot is excluded because the evidence describes personal flying interest and licensing rather than a defining professional pilot occupation. Property developer is excluded because the record shows investment exposure but does not establish a comparably defining practiced development role through a named owner-controlled development platform.

Official Riana Group descriptions of transaction totals and global reach are promotional and are not used as personal wealth estimates. No net-worth estimate or unsupported asset valuation is proposed.

Arab News describes Hawatt as Lebanese-Australian and another profile describes Lebanese family origins, but those formulations do not independently prove a second citizenship. Secondary nationality is therefore left unresolved.

No sufficiently strong source establishes a precise birth date, exact birthplace, middle names, suffix, secondary residence or personal website, so those fields remain unproposed. The exact LinkedIn and official Riana Group website are proposed; no collision-safe Instagram was found.

Forbes-first searches found no dedicated profile or reliably attributable article. Riana and all yacht, sale, price and brokerage material are excluded from the biographies, which remain source-invisible and centered on business mechanism.
